mechanism: undocumented workflow-warning skip key of unknown provenance; ultracode also suppresses the warning
mechanismB: provenance unknown: undocumented guardrail-disabling key in user settings
coverageNotes: settings-effective would surface the key and its file but label it 'not a known settings key', which reads as inert although the harness honors it; no tool says what it suppresses or which session wrote it. The workflows doc says a first Yes in auto mode 'records consent in your user settings' without naming the key (https://code.claude.com/docs/en/workflows).

mechanism: settings.json left unparseable mid-session; file silently skipped
mechanismB: parse error: settings.json made invalid mid-session, silently not applied
coverageNotes: The invalid JSON is caught whenever someone runs claude doctor, /doctor or settings-effective after the edit; Claude Code itself reports a Settings Error only at the next interactive start, so the mid-session fail-open is caught only on demand. The 'protective-looking' key was sandbox.credentials, which is documented (settings-reference, added 2.1.187), so its failure to block the read, and the Read-vs-Bash gap, are runtime issues no static tool sees.

mechanism: /model save-as-default rewrote settings.json from a stale snapshot, dropping hooks
mechanismB: harness rewrite: /model save-as-default wrote a stale settings snapshot, dropping hooks
coverageNotes: Only a before-and-after comparison catches this; the reporter found it in the git history of a dotfiles repo. Built-in and third-party listings show the current hooks, so the loss is visible only by absence, and agentshield flags it only if each guard hook was pre-declared in a policy.

resolution: Both classifiers say detectable. The conflict (the same servers in both enabled and disabled lists; rejection wins) is visible in the files regardless of who wrote it, so D2, first in rubric order.
mechanism: harness wrote .mcp.json servers into disabledMcpjsonServers (rejection beats enable)
mechanismB: harness rewrite: background launch wrote .mcp.json servers into disabledMcpjsonServers
coverageNotes: Tools show the servers as disabled but present it as a normal state. None flags that the same names sit in both lists or that the state changed after the user approved the servers.

resolution: Conservative. The changed file is a hook script, outside the protocol's checker file scope. Only one of the report's three variants would be caught even by fingerprinting scripts.
mechanism: hook script at wired path overwritten or stale under unchanged settings
mechanismB: outside config: hook script overwritten, stale or unresolved while settings unchanged
coverageNotes: All three variants (same-named script overwritten, stale installed copy, shim that resolves nothing) need the resolved target plus a content hash compared with a source or baseline; no listed tool does that. /hooks and settings-effective answer only one of the reporter's four asks: which settings file a row came from.

mechanism: project settings.json in an ancestor directory not loaded
mechanismB: load location: .claude/settings.json in an ancestor directory is never read
coverageNotes: Documented: 'Claude Code reads the shared .claude/settings.json from the session's primary working directory' (https://code.claude.com/docs/en/settings). Every tool shows the hooks and deny rules as missing only by absence; none reports the skipped ancestor file, which is the one warning the reporter asked for.

mechanism: allow rules cannot pre-approve writes to protected .claude/ paths
mechanismB: precedence: allow rules cannot pre-approve protected paths (~/.claude/)
coverageNotes: Documented at https://code.claude.com/docs/en/permission-modes#protected-paths: 'permissions.allow rules in settings files do not pre-approve protected-path writes.' No tool flags an allow rule that targets a protected path, and the native view shows it as in effect.

mechanism: agent frontmatter used skill field allowed-tools instead of tools
mechanismB: unknown key: allowed-tools in agent frontmatter instead of tools
coverageNotes: Documented semantics: tools is the agent field, unknown fields are ignored silently, and an omitted tools list inherits every tool (https://code.claude.com/docs/en/sub-agents). agentshield would give false reassurance here by crediting allowed-tools as a restriction.

mechanism: bare plugin-local agent: reference unresolved (plugin agents are namespaced)
mechanismB: missing reference: skill agent: names a bare plugin agent that does not resolve
coverageNotes: Anthropic confirmed the silent fallback as a bug on the issue. Plugin agents are named <plugin>:<name> (https://code.claude.com/docs/en/plugins/components#agents), so a checker could resolve bare names; /tasks, outside the protocol's list, shows the model on a subagent's row.

mechanism: Bash deny rule not enforced in auto mode
mechanismB: product bug: permissions.deny not enforced in auto mode
coverageNotes: The docs say allow, ask and deny rules resolve before the classifier in auto mode (https://code.claude.com/docs/en/permission-modes, 'How the classifier evaluates actions'), so this is a runtime bug that static tools can't see. Two tools show the rule as protective.

mechanism: agent frontmatter hooks: [] (array, not mapping) drops the agent
mechanismB: invalid value: hooks: [] in agent frontmatter silently drops the agent
coverageNotes: The agent shows up only by its absence from /context and from '--agent <name> not found. Available agents: ...'. Whether claude plugin validate catches the array type is undocumented; the docs' list of subagent files Claude Code skips does not include this case.

mechanism: .mcp.json ${VAR} from settings env not expanded; server silently dropped
mechanismB: product bug: settings env not applied to .mcp.json ${VAR} expansion; server silently dropped
coverageNotes: Version-specific: on 2.1.138 the REPL dropped the server silently and /mcp said 'No MCP servers configured'; current docs describe a named warning instead. Whether a settings env block feeds ${VAR} expansion in .mcp.json is still undocumented.

resolution: Both classifiers say not detectable. The report doesn't say which subagent type was used, so the documented behavior can't be applied.
mechanism: subagents without project CLAUDE.md/rules (agent type unknown)
mechanismB: product behavior: subagents did not load CLAUDE.md or .claude/rules (since changed)
coverageNotes: Current docs: Explore and Plan skip CLAUDE.md, and custom subagents load it unless they set omitClaudeMd (https://code.claude.com/docs/en/debug-your-config, 'Subagent ignores CLAUDE.md instructions'). No listed tool reports a subagent's loaded context, so the gap could not have been seen before the audit ran.

mechanism: auto_review reviewer approves sandbox escalations in codex exec
mechanismB: approval semantics: auto_review approves sandbox escalations, so --sandbox read-only is not a hard boundary
coverageNotes: Codex docs say auto_review 'evaluates only actions that already need approval, such as sandbox escalations' (https://developers.openai.com/codex/agent-approvals-security), but nothing warns an exec caller that the read-only level no longer binds.

mechanism: AGENTS.md beyond project_doc_max_bytes (32 KiB) truncated
mechanismB: size limit: AGENTS.md truncated at project_doc_max_bytes
coverageNotes: The 32 KiB limit is documented ('stops adding files once the combined size reaches ... project_doc_max_bytes (32 KiB by default)'). Truncation is logged, not shown; the docs also suggest asking Codex to summarize its instructions, which is a model self-report.

mechanism: code review custom instructions without observable effect (cause unknown)
mechanismB: insufficient information: instructions without observable effect in code review
coverageNotes: No validator checks .instructions.md frontmatter either: the report's excludeAgent: "coding-agent" is not one of the values the docs list ('code-review' or 'cloud-agent'), and nothing would say so.

mechanism: cloud agent skips copilot-instructions.md in organization-owned repos
mechanismB: product bug: cloud agent never fetches copilot-instructions.md in org-owned repos
coverageNotes: A difference between org-owned and personal repositories in the hosted agent; no static check applies. The session log shows it only while or after the agent runs.

mechanism: MCP tools hidden in runtime virtual tool groups
mechanismB: insufficient information: MCP tool groups built at runtime
coverageNotes: The commenter's gap (tool groups not listable by the agent or the user) has no documented diagnostic.

resolution: Secondary analysis only. Cursor's docs say MCP config works the same in the CLI and the editor and list no type values, so the CLI's rejection contradicts the docs: a bug, not a schema violation.
mechanism: CLI rejects mcp.json type 'streamable-http' and drops the whole file
mechanismB: invalid value: MCP transport type streamable-http rejected by the CLI
coverageNotes: Cursor's IDE accepts the value and its CLI rejects the whole file; both third-party tools model the IDE, so they would pass the config.

mechanism: team rule names containing '/' cannot be disabled locally
mechanismB: product bug: team rule with '/' in its name ignores the local opt-out
coverageNotes: No documented view lists the rules actually sent to the model; the reporter asked the agent. Cursor staff traced it to rule names containing '/'.

mechanism: alwaysApply in team-plugin rules downgraded to agent-requestable
mechanismB: product bug: alwaysApply ignored for team-plugin rules
coverageNotes: Confirmed Cursor bug, fixed in 3.6 per staff. The built-in panel shows the downgrade but not that it contradicts the file.

mechanism: 'Always allow' written to global config, shadowed by project permissions
mechanismB: product bug: grant written to global config and shadowed by project permissions
coverageNotes: Cursor staff: an empty or partial project permissions block overrides the global allow list during merge, so the global grant never applies. Nothing shows the effective list.

mechanism: Cursor CLI imports Claude Code hooks/agents/rules with no opt-out
mechanismB: cross-tool scope: cursor-agent loads Claude Code and Codex config with no CLI opt-out
coverageNotes: Cursor staff agreed the IDE's third-party toggle doesn't reach the CLI; no tool shows what the CLI imports.

resolution: The installer added a hook entry to a user settings file the checker reads. A last-seen baseline comparison flags the new entry on the next run, before the uninstall left it dangling.
mechanism: leftover third-party hook rewrites commands to a removed binary
mechanismB: third-party tool write: installer added a hook to user settings, left behind after uninstall
coverageNotes: Native views surface the stale hook, not the failure (a hook calling a binary that is gone). Catching it needs command resolution inside the hook script.

resolution: Classifier A read the screenshot, which shows ask rules Bash(rm:*) and Bash(rmdir:*). The permissions docs say 'a matching ask rule still prompts even when the hook returned "allow"' (verified in the docs). Classifier B read an archive copy without the image.
mechanism: ask rules override a PreToolUse hook's allow decision
mechanismB: insufficient information: hook failure with cause not reported
coverageNotes: Documented: for PreToolUse, 'Deny and ask rules are still evaluated regardless of what the hook returns' (https://code.claude.com/docs/en/hooks). The post's screenshot shows the ask rules overriding the hook's allow; no tool flags a hook decision shadowed by an ask rule.

mechanism: single-slash 'absolute' path in Read deny rules anchors at settings source
mechanismB: path anchoring: single-slash Read/Grep deny rules are not absolute paths
coverageNotes: Documented: 'A pattern like /Users/alice/file isn't an absolute path. The single leading slash anchors at the settings source ... Use //Users/alice/file' (https://code.claude.com/docs/en/permissions#read-and-edit). Claude Code's own startup warning covers Write, NotebookEdit, MultiEdit and Glob path rules, not this case (https://code.claude.com/docs/en/errors).

mechanism: marketplace errors caused CLI to wipe project settings.json
mechanismB: harness rewrite: project .claude/settings.json wiped after marketplace errors
coverageNotes: The wipe is harness-initiated drift; nothing compares .claude/settings.json with a committed or last-seen copy. Validate helps only by preventing the trigger.

mechanism: nested CLAUDE.md lazy-loads only on Read; auto mode's Bash-first skips it
mechanismB: load condition / matcher scope: lazy nested CLAUDE.md and Edit|Write hooks bypassed by Bash
coverageNotes: The on-demand loading rule is documented; the Bash-first auto mode instruction the post measured is not. Only a live /context check, by absence, shows the missing file; the hook bypass is not surfaced.
